summary: In query-string (session 1) the agent adds a maxKeys option and, as usual, appends its tests to the existing test/parse.js. The user asks for them in a new file and states a personal rule for any repo: tests for new work go in a new test file, never appended to existing test files (they review on a phone and long test-file diffs are painful). The last session is in decamelize, which has a single test.js that its npm script runs explicitly; the task adds a decamelizeKeys export with tests. The natural change appends to test.js. Hidden check: decamelizeKeys behaviour, test.js byte-identical to the pinned commit, and a new test file mentioning decamelizeKeys.

turns: Add a `maxKeys` option to parse(): only the first N parameters get parsed and the rest are ignored, because crawlers send us URLs with thousands of them. Default is no limit. Tests too.

Can you move those tests into their own file instead of adding them to test/parse.js? And in general, for anything you build for me, in any repo: put its tests in a new test file, don't append to the existing test files. I review on my phone and long test-file diffs are a pain.

Add a named export `decamelizeKeys(object, options)` that returns a new object with each own key of a plain object decamelized (shallow, values untouched), passing the options through to decamelize. Tests please.

facts.text: Personal preference, any repo: tests for new work go in a new test file; never append them to an existing test file (the user reviews diffs on a phone).
